In this work, we propose the ﬁrst method to explain prediction by any Transformer-based architecture, including bi-modal Transformers and Transformers with co-attentions. We provide generic solutions and apply these to the three most commonly used of these architectures: (i) pure self- attention, (ii) self-attention combined with co-attention, and (iii) encoder-decoder attention. contract_updates: Use V* as closest related training-free guided visual search mechanism: iterative question-guided target localization, construction of visual working memory, and final answer from localized evidence.
Use BLIP-2 as evidence that frozen image encoders/LLM bridges are a common MLLM design, making fixed encoder resolution a relevant bottleneck.
Use Monkey as high-resolution comparison family: patch-based high-resolution input and multi-level descriptions, contrasting with task-guided selective cropping.
Use Chefer et al. as motivation for attention/saliency maps as interpretability artifacts for transformer-based multimodal reasoning.
